Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

types.embedding_query_text: CountryName: A proper noun or phrase used to identify a specific country. Also called Nation name, Geographical name, Place name, Territory designation. Examples: Aotearoa.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Country' class represents the entity identified by a country name like 'Aotearoa'.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

types.embedding_query_text: LocationType: A general classification for a kind of place or venue. Also called Venue type, Place category, Setting type, Area classification. Examples: courtrooms.

chosen_type.label: LocationType
chosen_type.definition: A general classification for a kind of place or venue.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a general 'LocationType' as a classification; 'Enumeration' is the closest parent for a category.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

types.embedding_query_text: Website: A set of related web pages typically identified with a common domain name and published on at least one web server. Also called Web portal, Online platform, Internet site, Web presence. Examples: UK government website.

chosen_type.label: WebSite
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'WebSite' class directly matches the OIE type and its example.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: ContactPage
candidates.comment: A web page specifically designed to provide contact information for an entity. Also called contact us page, inquiry page, reach us page. Examples: A website's "Contact Us" page, a business's support page, a personal portfolio's contact section. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.

candidates.label: AboutPage
candidates.comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence. Also called Record, Report, Text, File. Examples: report.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Report' class directly matches the OIE type's example 'report'.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided. Also called Calendar month, Lunar cycle, Period, Interval. Examples: June.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class specifically represents a 'Month'; 'Duration' is the closest parent for a period of time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Argument: A reason or set of reasons given with the aim of persuading others that an action or idea is right or wrong. Also called Reasoning, Justification, Claim, Assertion. Examples: unnecessary use of resources, unnecessary division within society, undermining the two other official languages, waste of time.

chosen_type.label: Statement
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'Statement' class, representing a declaration or assertion, is the best fit for the examples of arguments or points made.

mentions: undermining the two other official languages
clarify the long-accepted status of English
recognize in legislation what has long been assumed in New Zealand

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: UserComments
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting comments or feedback. Also called user comment, public comment, feedback post. Examples: a user leaving a comment on a blog post, posting a review, providing feedback on a product.

types.embedding_query_text: LanguageGroup: A classification of languages that share common characteristics or are spoken by a particular demographic. Also called Language family, Linguistic group, Dialect cluster, Speech community. Examples: minority languages, those minority languages.

chosen_type.label: LanguageGroup
chosen_type.definition: A classification of languages that share common characteristics or are spoken by a particular demographic.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a 'LanguageGroup'; 'Intangible' is suitable for an abstract concept like a group of languages.

candidates.label: Language
candidates.comment: Language is an intangible representing natural languages such as Spanish or English, distinct from programming languages. Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language. Examples: English, Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic. Distinct from ComputerLanguage, which refers to programming languages.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalStatus: The position or standing of a person, entity, or concept in the eyes of the law. Also called Legal standing, Judicial position, Lawful condition, Rights and obligations. Examples: stronger rights.

chosen_type.label: LegalStatus
chosen_type.definition: The position or standing of a person, entity, or concept in the eyes of the law.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a general 'LegalStatus'; 'StatusEnumeration' is the closest parent for a type of status.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: DrugLegalStatus
candidates.comment: A DrugLegalStatus is a MedicalIntangible indicating the legal availability status of a medical drug. Also called medication legal standing, pharmaceutical regulatory status. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter, ControlledSubstance.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

types.embedding_query_text: LegalContext: The specific circumstances or environment within which legal actions or discussions occur. Also called Legal setting, Judicial environment, Court context, Legal framework. Examples: legal proceedings.

chosen_type.label: LegalContext
chosen_type.definition: The specific circumstances or environment within which legal actions or discussions occur.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a 'LegalContext'; 'Intangible' is suitable for an abstract environment.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: Status: The relative social, professional, or other standing of someone or something. Also called Position, Standing, Rank, Condition. Examples: long-accepted status.

chosen_type.label: StatusEnumeration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org 'StatusEnumeration' class directly matches the general concept of 'Status'.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: GameServerStatus
candidates.comment: A GameServerStatus is a StatusEnumeration representing the operational status of a game server. Also called server status, game server state. Examples: Online, Offline, Maintenance.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

types.embedding_query_text: Consequence: A result or effect of an action or condition. Also called Outcome, Result, Effect, Repercussion. Examples: little harm.

chosen_type.label: Outcome
chosen_type.definition: The way a thing turns out; a consequence or result.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a 'Consequence' as a result or effect; 'Intangible' is suitable for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOrder: A directive or command issued by a government authority. Also called Decree, Edict, Mandate, Proclamation. Examples: executive order.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrder
chosen_type.definition: A directive or command issued by a government authority.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class directly represents a 'GovernmentOrder' like an 'executive order'; 'Legislation' is the closest parent for a legal directive.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: Order
candidates.comment: An Order is an intangible entity representing a confirmation of a transaction, containing accepted offers as line items. Also called purchase order, sales order, receipt. Examples: an online shopping order confirmation, a restaurant bill, a service agreement. Distinct from Offer, which is a proposal before acceptance.

types.embedding_query_text: PoliticalAlignment Examples: left-wing.

chosen_type.label: PoliticalAlignment
chosen_type.definition: A position or orientation within a political spectrum.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents 'PoliticalAlignment'; 'Intangible' is suitable for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: PoliticalIdeology Examples: nationalist.

chosen_type.label: PoliticalIdeology
chosen_type.definition: A set of beliefs and principles that guides an individual or group's political actions and goals.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents 'PoliticalIdeology'; 'Intangible' is suitable for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.
